summary: RADIUS NAC VLAN misattribution: EAP authentication succeeds but guest VLAN applied, blocking VPN onboarding
description:
Issue summary:
Users on corporate Wi‑Fi intermittently finish 802.1X/EAP authentication but are placed into the guest VLAN by the NAC server. Devices in guest VLAN cannot complete VPN onboarding (agent registration + device cert fetch), causing blocked access to internal services and failed onboarding flows for new hires and reprovisioned devices.

Impact:
- Affects ~12% of onboarding attempts in corp Wi‑Fi during business hours in us-east-1; affects both macOS and Windows devices.
- New hire device provisioning fails to retrieve device certs; SSO flows time out.
- Customer-facing demo environment unreachable when presenters use corp Wi‑Fi.

Environment:
- SSID: Redwood-Corp-Enterprise (802.1X, WPA2/WPA3 transition)
- NAC: ClearAccess v4.2 (RADIUS proxy + policy engine)
- RADIUS backend: FreeRADIUS cluster behind haproxy (auth and CoA)
- Identity provider: Okta SSO -> RADIUS proxy (EAP-TLS and EAP-PEAP tested)
- VPN: WireGuard-based zero-trust agent with onboarding over TLS to onboarding.redwood.internal:443
- Affected clients: macOS 13.x, Windows 11 x64, occasionally Linux dev VMs

Steps to reproduce:
1) Connect client to Redwood-Corp-Enterprise SSID and authenticate with EAP-PEAP (username/password) or EAP-TLS cert.
2) Observe RADIUS authentication logs show Accept for user/device.
3) Confirm client gets DHCP & IP on guest VLAN (192.168.240.0/22) instead of corp VLAN (10.20.0.0/16).
4) Attempt agent registration to onboarding.redwood.internal:443 -> connection times out; cert fetch fails.

Observed behavior / logs (excerpt):
- RADIUS server: "Auth: Accept: user=ajones realm=redwood internal="
- NAC policy engine audit: "PolicyDecision: TAG=guest_vlans; assignment=192.168.240.0/22; reason=policy-match: device-profile=unknown, posture=unscanned"
- DHCP logs: "DHCPACK yiaddr=192.168.240.55 to MAC aa:bb:cc:dd:ee:ff via VLAN 240"
- Onboarding server logs: "TLS handshake from 192.168.240.55 timed out; client failed to present expected bootstrap cert"

Hypothesis:
- NAC policy mis-evaluates posture for successfully authenticated devices causing fallback to guest VLAN when device posture check times out or returns unknown.
- Intermittent timeouts between NAC and posture service (hosted on separate k8s namespace) cause race where authentication completes before posture result arrives, leading to default-to-guest behavior.
- A mismatch in RADIUS CoA handling may fail to move some sessions after posture completes.

Investigation notes:
- 2026-03-12 09:15 (Diego): Correlated increased rates with periodic posture-service GC spikes; saw 5–7s latency spikes in posture API during rolling node autoscaling.
- 2026-03-12 10:02 (Priya): Captured packet trace from AP showing Access-Accept followed by RADIUS Change-of-Auth not applied for session 0x7a3f.
- 2026-03-12 11:30 (SRE): Hapoxy logs show occasional 503s to posture-service endpoints during scale events; backlog of requests queued.
- 2026-03-12 12:00 (Network Eng): NAC policy has explicit default assignment to guest VLAN when posture result absent after 3s.
- 2026-03-12 12:45 (Security): Reviewed recent NAC policy change (#472) that lowered posture hold-time to 3s to reduce auth latency for BYOD; this increases chance of defaulting to guest.

Temporary workaround applied:
- 2026-03-12 13:10 (Priya): Increased posture hold-time back to 8s via runtime flag on NAC policy engine cluster (deployed config patch ci-ops/patch-2026-03-12).
- 2026-03-12 13:15 (SRE): Scaled posture-service HPA min replicas from 2 -> 4 to reduce tail latency.
- Result: Guest VLAN misassignment rate dropped from ~12% to ~1.5% in the monitoring window (10:00–14:00).

Next steps and action items:
- Short term (Priority): Patch NAC policy repo to set posture hold-time to 8s permanently and add feature flag gating (#priv-ops-553). Owner: Priya Shah. ETA: 2026-03-14.
- Medium term: Improve posture-service autoscaling to rely on CPU+queue length and add readiness probe to avoid sending requests during GC/scale windows. Owner: SRE team (linked PRs). ETA: 2026-03-21.
- Long term: Update onboarding flow to support re-provisioning via HTTP proxy fallback when devices land in guest VLAN temporarily and to support CoA retries when posture completes. Owner: Security/Infra. ETA: Q2 2026.

Attachments: packet captures, haproxy logs, NAC policy audit snippets available in linked Confluence page and s3://redwood-support/INT-531234/
comments: 2026-03-12 09:40 - Diego Ramos: Initial customer reports came in via #internal-support. Noticed pattern of Accept but guest VLAN. Opening ticket and grabbing logs.

2026-03-12 10:05 - Priya Shah: Pulled NAC audit logs. Policy shows fallback to guest when posture service does not return in 3s. Suspect recent change to reduce login latency. Adding SRE for posture API latency investigation.
2026-03-12 11:45 - SRE Team (sre-oncall): Found GC spikes on posture-service causing 5–10s tail latency. Scaling to 4 replicas reduced error rates. We recommend increasing hold-time on NAC.

2026-03-12 13:20 - Priya Shah: Temporarily increased NAC posture hold-time to 8s and bumped posture-service HPA. Monitoring shows misassignment rate decreased ~10x. Preparing patch for NAC policy repo to make change permanent.

2026-03-12 17:05 - Security (Amira Liao): Confirmed this change reduces risk of leaving corporate devices in guest VLAN. We should document CoA retry behavior and add test coverage for posture latencies.

2026-03-13 09:00 - Diego Ramos: Noted two remaining edge cases where devices behind some AP firmware versions didn't accept CoA reassignments; network team will test AP firmware 5.7.2+ compatibility with CoA.
2026-03-13 15:20 - Priya Shah: Created config PR ci-configs/nac/patch-553 and linked PR in infra-config. Marking ticket In Progress while change undergoes code review and staging deployment.
investigation: Timeline shows correlation between posture-service latency spikes and spike in guest VLAN assignments.
Haproxy logs show 503s to posture endpoints during cluster GC/resize windows.
Packet capture demonstrates Access-Accept followed by no CoA and DHCP assignment on guest net.
Recent change lowered posture hold-time to 3s; revert to 8s reduces misassignments.
Noticed AP firmware 5.6.x had inconsistent CoA behavior; recommend upgrade to 5.7.2+ where CoA handling improved.
resolution: Temporary mitigation: increased NAC posture hold-time to 8s and scaled posture-service to reduce tail latency (2026-03-12).

Permanent fix in progress: PR created to update NAC policy repo to 8s hold-time and add configurable default behavior; add regression test for posture latency windows. Owner: Priya Shah. ETA 2026-03-14 deployment to staging.
SRE will implement improved HPA metrics and readiness probe for posture-service to avoid serving during GC/scale events. Owner: SRE. ETA 2026-03-21.
Network team to validate CoA handling on AP firmware 5.7.2+ and schedule upgrade for devices still on 5.6.x.
